newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Squeeze tightens in nearby European soymeal -trade.
newsitem.headline: Squeeze tightens in nearby European soymeal -trade.

text.p: A tightening squeeze has developed on the nearby positions in soybeanmeal in Europe due to late soybean crop arrivals from the United States, which has delayed crushing operations in Europe, traders said.

The tightness was exacerbated on Friday by a firm close to business in Chicago futures and helped to push up seller prices for South American soymeal by $2.00 to $5.00 a tonne on Monday morning, depending on the position.
Dutch high protein soymeal benefited strongly as one of the available alternatives, soaring between $3 and $11 a tonne.

Traders said the situation was not abnormal for the time of year as the South American shipments were slowing and the late U.S. crop meant shipments from there had yet to get underway in earnest. But it was causing problems for some in the trade.
Although ships carrying material have been arriving at European ports, most of the cargoes have already been bought.
"There is little unsold soymeal arriving into Europe at the moment," one trader said, adding there were still some operators who needed to cover positions.
"It could be alarming for those who need to cover their nearby needs," one trader said.

Arrivals were beginning to increase and the tightness was viewed a temporary situation but traders were waiting to see how much would be available for the nearby market. Around six vessels carrying South American soymeal are due in northern Europe in the next two weeks.
Traders said the arrival of controversial genetically-altered soybeans into Europe had not had any impact on the market yet.
